subject.title: feat(slack): support running as a real Slack user (user identity)

question: Should OpenClaw support a Slack account running with a human OAuth token and a companion app for event delivery after live DM/MPIM proof is supplied?
rationale: This is an intentional expansion of credential authority and channel behavior, so tests alone cannot determine the repository's acceptable security and product boundary.

options.title: Require live proof and owner approval
options.body: Obtain redacted evidence for inbound DM/MPIM delivery, self-event suppression, and outbound posting, then have the Slack/security owner approve the user-token boundary.

options.title: Decline human-token identity mode
options.body: Keep Slack limited to bot identity if maintainers do not want OpenClaw to operate under a personal Slack OAuth identity.

recommendation.title: Require live proof and owner approval
recommendation.body: Obtain redacted evidence for inbound DM/MPIM delivery, self-event suppression, and outbound posting, then have the Slack/security owner approve the user-token boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Slack monitor and gateway work makes this person the strongest available routing candidate for the implementation and boundary decision.
